topics.title: AC voltage applied to a resistor

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the phase relation between current and voltage in a resistor and why it heats up although the average current is zero.
Relate rms and peak values of alternating current and voltage and use them to find average power in a resistor.

topics.title: Representation of ac current and voltage by phasors

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret a phasor as a rotating vector whose length is the amplitude and whose vertical projection is the instantaneous value.
Explain why voltages that are out of phase must be combined using phasors rather than added algebraically.

topics.title: AC voltage applied to an inductor

concepts.learning_objective: Use X_L = omega L to find the current through a pure inductor and predict how it changes with frequency.
State that current lags voltage by pi/2 in a pure inductor and explain why the average power over a cycle is zero.

topics.title: AC voltage applied to a capacitor

concepts.learning_objective: Use X_C = 1/(omega C) to find the current through a capacitor and predict how it changes with frequency.
State that current leads voltage by pi/2 in a capacitor and that no average power is consumed by it.

topics.title: AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit and resonance

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the impedance and current of a series LCR circuit using the phasor (impedance) diagram.
Find the resonant frequency of a series LCR circuit and analyse the current and voltages at resonance.

topics.title: Power in ac circuit: the power factor

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate average power as P = V I cos(phi) and explain the effect of power factor on transmission losses.
Explain wattless current and how a capacitor improves the power factor of an inductive load.
State that a transformer works on mutual induction and needs a changing magnetic flux.
Apply V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p and I_s/I_p = N_p/N_s and explain why power is transmitted at high voltage.
Identify the energy losses in a real transformer and how each is reduced.
